items.summary: The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for y
items.content:
The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for your listening pleasure on major streaming platforms. "Devourer," was first heard during the Epoch Operation: Taubound Official Gameplay Teaser. Influenced by slow, heavy metal from the likes of Black Sabbath, it features lyrics "sung" in Voidtongue, the terrifyingly enigmatic language of the Untime. This was a deliberate choice, recalling the memorable moment from 2023's Whispers in the Walls Quest when you took control of one of Albrecht Entrati's Vessels for the first time. Here, these elements combine for a musical experience that feels as massive and imposing as your latest endeavors ahead of Warframe: Tau, coming later this year.

Where can I listen?

You can listen to "Devourer" on:

  • Apple Music

items.title: ‘Warframe’ “Epoch Operation: Taubound” Event Live
items.summary: Late last week, Digital Extremes announced their latest event "Epoch Operation: Taubound" for their long-running sci-fi free-to-play looter shooter title
items.content:
Mobile News Nintendo PC PlayStation Xbox Genghis Husameddin

Late last week, Digital Extremes announced their latest event “Epoch Operation: Taubound” for their long-running sci-fi free-to-play looter shooter title ‘Warframe’—beckoning players to hop into the game’s monumental community event prior to the launch of “Tau”. New and returning players can tackle activities before Tuesday, 17 November, earning event rewards and collect resources to fuel the course to a new Star System, while diving back into The Lotus’ memories in a narrative Prologue Quest—Prologue to Tau.

The limited-time Epoch Operation: Taubound community event is comprised of two parts, a global objective to work towards, and a new narrative Prologue Quest:

Seek out greater challenges with the recently launched six-player mission type, The Icebind : Head to Yuvan Peak and recruit five other friends to form a squad of six, each with only one type of Warframe , for a new kind of game mode requiring heightened cooperation and teamwork. Offer up one Cryobell key per squadmate and vote on which set of randomized modifiers, like enemy faction, level layout, mission objectives, and potential debuffs, the team will need to overcome together. Coordinate strategies across four different phases and earn one of dozens of treasures to pick from Melica’s Glacial Laboratory upon completion.

“It’s no small task to travel the void of space toward an entirely new Star System, but I know the Warframe community is up for the challenge,” said Megan Everett , Community Director. “Community is our nexus. Our players are our champions. And so we call to them, new and returning, for this incredibly special time in Warframe’ s storied history, to rise to the occasion and reach for new stars. Together, we will discover what has become of Tau.”

Warframe is available across PC via Warframe.com /Steam (Windows & Linux via Proton), Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch consoles, iOS, and Android devices. Full cross-save and crossplay are supported across all platforms. And again, Warframe’s Tau update will be coming this way very soon.

Enjoying DayOne ? Do us a favour, and make us a ‘ Preferred Source on Google ‘ – that way, you’ll only be delivered more gaming coverage from our team.

There’s plenty of ways to become a part of DayOne. Head over and let us know your thoughts in the Day O ne Forums , the perfect place to chat about games if you’re a little more old-school and prefer things in a longform form, and if you mainly play on PC, join our Steam Community to connect with other members and maybe make some new friends!

Prefer the chaos of live and fast moving conversation? Come and make some noise in the lively DayOne Community Discord Server instead. If you’re rocking a DayOne Membership, both places give special access for our supporters, and you’ll unlock a ton of exclusive content, just for you.

items.title: How to play the Prologue to Tau quest in Warframe
items.content:
How to play the Prologue to Tau quest in Warframe One of the late-game warriors.

Anyone can jump into the new Taubound event, but the Prologue to Tau mission is harder to access. This one is for the vets, and you'll need to have put in the hours if you want to experience it for yourself. The good news is that, unlike the event itself, this quest will stick around, so even if you cannot play it now, you will be able to once you get far enough into the game.

To play this quest, you need to have completed The Old Peace and The Hex story quests, the two most recent quests in the game. If you have done that, and go visit your Codex on your ship, you will be able to access the new Prologue Quest and Chapters section, Prologue to Tau.

I don't want to get into spoiler territory, but it's definitely a first for Warframe to have you do what you do in this quest. Once you wrap up the quest, you will be awarded the Taubound Honoria. After that, you can crack on with Epoch Operation: Taubound and start paving the way to the next chapter of Warframe.

If you found this guide useful, b e sure to check out our Warframe page for more helpful guides.

items.title: Warframe Sets Course for a Distant Star System in Epoch Operation: Taubound
items.summary: In Epoch Operation: Taubound, new and returning XBOX players are invited to jump into missions on Eris in The Origin System, where they’ll destroy Infested enemies and obtain a new resource — Moonflesh.
items.content:
Community is the nexus of everything we do and every choice we make as Warframe developers. We create games with players, not just for players, and build trust over time through actions that demonstrate we listen. Our players around the world in our XBOX community are a monumental part of that family portrait; they help us make Warframe a better experience for everyone, and they deliver the critical feedback we need to ensure Warframe remains a safe, enjoyable space to spend a little time with friends and family online. To this day, I still pull out my XBOX 360 controller for our live TennoCon demos — it’s one of my favorite peripherals of all time.

Since Warframe debuted on XBOX One in 2014, we’ve thrived on stories and reports from our welcoming community of players across two generations of XBOX. In that time, we’ve brought them parity in content across platforms, introduced new ways to engage with a more global community with the introduction of cross-play and cross-save, and have dedicated platform-specific resources for players on XBOX to communicate with us directly.

From fan art, to handwritten thank-you letters, to bug reports and the constructive criticism we need to improve the experience day after day, and year after year, our XBOX community gives us the medicine we need to be stronger, smarter, and more inclusive. And we’re certainly not done yet.

From Warframe’s humble beginnings, we’ve teased the far-future narrative of Tau, a distant Star System shrouded in mystery. This year, we’re finally going together, and our community of XBOX players can help us get there. Alongside millions of players worldwide, we invite the community to join us in Epoch Operation: Taubound , arriving in Warframe on October 15. This unique, one-time community event will rally players everywhere, anywhere, for the ultimate cooperative challenge: fuel the trip to the distant Star System, Tau. Participation will be rewarded, and XBOX players won’t want to miss out before the event concludes on November 17.

In Epoch Operation: Taubound, new and returning XBOX players are invited to jump into missions on Eris in The Origin System, where they’ll destroy Infested enemies and obtain a new resource — Moonflesh — to power up the Sentient Mothership, Praghasa , and trade this curious new resource for event rewards. Coveted event rewards highlight what players on XBOX can discover and unlock alongside the community, including brand-new Armor Sets, exclusive event Honoria, Somachords, and other stunning cosmetics ranging from Glyphs, Sigils, Floofs, Syandanas, Signas, Badges, Blueprints, and so much more.

But that’s not all we have in store for our XBOX community. Also arriving is Prologue to Tau, a bite-sized entry in our single-player cinematic quest campaign that invites players to go hands-on with The Lotus for the first time ever (as seen during TennoLIVE 2026), setting the narrative stakes for this next monumental chapter in Warframe . Players can also finally use their Vessel they customized during TennoCon on the surface of Eris in a unique level and face off in a massive Infested boss fight. These permanent additions to Warframe ’s Quest Codex are not time-limited and are available to XBOX players who have completed The Hex and The Old Peace Quests.

From Tau and back, we are incredibly thankful to our XBOX community for being a part of this journey for 13+ years, and we look forward to the adventures ahead with you.

items.title: I Underestimated The New Icebind Game Mode in Warframe – Opinion
items.summary: The new Icebind game mode in Warframe is an excellent new idea that finally launched after being delayed, here is a critique of it.
items.content:
A couple of days ago, I wrote an article venting my frustrations and disappointment in the recent update in Warframe , the Iceblade of Narin. Having the grind for her and her weapons locked to already existing game modes with their own loot pools, bloating the drop chances, felt like a miss to me. All the while, the way it was the send-off update before we ramp up for Tau felt a little underwhelming overall. In a recent update, Digital Extremes added the endgame game mode that was delayed, the “Icebind,” and it fixes one problem I had listed in that previous article, and another longstanding issue with Digital Extremes’ approach to endgame content, while also adding a few issues of its own.

The Icebind is the newest game mode in Warframe that was originally delayed from the Iceblade of Narin update . It is a 6-player, endgame-focused activity that requires manually inviting people to do it. The Icebind has 4 different game modes you can choose from, including:

How this game mode differs is set modifiers and very harsh conditions, including enemies at level 999 and above. As well as only allows one player to use a specific warframe in the squad. This means that you cannot stack 5 Dantes and a Harrow to avoid every harsh condition. This game mode also opts for additional side objectives that, if you start and fail, you fail the mission overall. Completing the side objectives gives you extra keys to acquire loot at the end of the mission.

With all of this out in the open, how does this game mode actually land? Well, I think it lands very well on its own two feet and feels much more rewarding and enjoyable as opposed to the weekly Archimedea runs that have become feeling a little outdated. It is a refresh of the endgame approach for Warframe and one that is definitely welcome, so long as there are aims to improve it.

The Icebind puts 6 players into already existing game modes with side objectives, when I feel the new objectives could have been their own game modes altogether. The side objectives are an interesting mix of new ideas. For example, players have to stand in a line to link up power from one place to another. A giant ice shrine you need to do a lot of DPS to break the bubbles around it. Not to mention a bubble that marks areas around it that are safe and unsafe to jump around to avoid getting hit. And a chest that requires keys dropped by enemies to open by standing next to said chest.

They do not sound really interesting on their own, but they are fun in practice so long as players understand what they are doing. My biggest concern about the integration here is how these new objectives are just optional challenges in already existing game modes when they feel like they could have been mixed into one game mode that goes from one step to the next. For example, the power chain being the opening objective, then the orb with the little “Simon says” area around it following the chain, then leading into that DPS check with the ice shrine before needing to do the chest as the final objective to unlock extraction.

Obviously, I know making these objectives optional in the existing game modes made it easier for players to engage in. But if there are going to be more experimentation for endgame content with this type of stuff, a dedication to the new ideas as opposed to old ones would be a better way to go, to me at least. This game mode does correct one issue in the overall update, however. That being how Narin is integrated into the wider narrative.

In my previous article critiquing the general update, I mentioned how there was a complete absence of narrative integration for Narin. I was not aware that the integration would be worked into the Icebind, instead of a dedicated mission for when you are farming for Narin. It’s a subversion that I wasn’t expecting, but I do understand what Digital Extremes were going for now. The only little bit of inconsistency is the lack of the murmur.

Seeing as the Icebind makes references to the Hex and the Indifference worming its way further into the origin system. I feel the murmur should have been the only enemy for narrative cohesion. As it stands, however, it is better worked in now, and I feel better about the update overall. I do look forward to hearing more explanations as the weeks progress with the Icebind.

Finally, the rewards are weirdly misrepresented. When the rewards were shown off originally, I assumed stuff like the Kuva were going to be bad-luck RNG drops. As some of us know from sorties/archon hunts. Luckily, that is not the case. Every chest drops a random good item, like boosters, rivens, forma, etc on top of the Kuva. My only complaint about this system is having a singular forma in the same drop table as a forma bundle. Not to mention the Kuva amount from either drop feels low. I think adding some entropic Kuva to the drop tables would incentivise players more to get the cosmetics and other goodies from Melica.

Finally, the new Riven Splicers are great. I have zero complaints about how they function. I also appreciate that they are a guaranteed reward on top of everything earned in an Icebind run. This feature is an excellent overhaul to the Riven system for endgame players. Heck, my negative crit Phenmor riven has weak spot damage now. Which is a fantastically nasty combo with my Harrow.

With all of this out in the open. I would like to recommend that Digital Extremes keep going with this idea. I feel the Icebind is strangely more approachable than Archimedea right now. This is mostly due to the fact that they do not force you to play with frames and weapons you do not like or have proper builds for. Enticing players to use their best-of-the-best builds and weapons for singular mission runs is a great idea. I just feel like the objectives could be their own things. As well as touching up the reward pool for better consistency. As it stands, just asking for an Icebind group in recruitment chat or in Yuvan Peak works perfectly.

items.title: October in Warframe
items.summary: As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following e
items.content:
As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following events this month:

EPOCH OPERATION: TAUBOUND

October 15 - November 17 A unique event unlike anything you've experienced to date, Epoch Operation: Taubound offers all eligible Tenno the chance to become a part of Warframe history. If you want to help open up a path to the Tau System, be sure to have your account ready by completing the "Vor's Prize" Quest before October 15. Players looking to pilot their Vessel for the first time can also complete The Hex and The Old Peace in order to access a new, permanent Prologue Quest setting up the Road to Tau. For full event details – including prerequisites and more – click here.

NIGHTS OF NABERUS

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Spooky season returns to the Origin System during our annual Halloween-inspired event, with Daughter releasing her inventory of new and returning seasonal Customizations in exchange for Mother Tokens. While Baro Ki'Teer will mark the occasion in the same unsettling fashion as last year (IYKYK), we're also mixing it up by bringing back the Hallowed Nightmares Tactical Alert, allowing you to face off against the fearsome Jack O'Naut for even more Naberus treats. For all the harrowing details, check out our Halloween 2026 Events post.

NEW GAME MODE: THE ICEBIND

October 7 Originally intended to ship alongside Iceblade of Narin as "Glacial Defiance," our new 6-player game mode was ultimately delayed to allow for additional development time and renamed to The Icebind. Accessible in-game starting October 7, these challenging, high-level Missions can be played up to three times weekly, allowing you to put your teamwork (and Loadouts) to the test for valuable Rewards. Visit the official Warframe Forums to learn more about the delay, and further details of the game mode itself.

PRINCESS MARGARET CANCER FOUNDATION QUEST

October 1 - October 31 PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation light the way towards a world free from the fear of cancer. Visit the Warframe PMCF Quest webpage for more information or donate directly here.

items.title: Iceblade of Narin Official Soundtrack
items.summary: Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable So
items.content:
Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable Sound Team reverberates across the three tracks comprising this release. Drawing inspiration from a traditional Korean musical style called Sanjo, each song evokes the powerful, dynamic movements of a sword dancer — just like our 66th Warframe, Narin. The melodies recorded for Neote's Dance also inspired the vocals in Ice Speaker, which further combines familiar tunes associated with both the Zariman and the Man in the Wall for a unique aural motif befitting the narrative strands threaded through our latest update (as well as the intensity of the upcoming Glacial Defiance game mode).

items.title: Destiny’s biggest rival Warframe has had ‘two years of massive growth’
items.summary: Digital Extremes believes in console growth, and discusses the ‘careful’ development of its second game
items.content:
Playback speed × Share post Share post at current time Share from 0:00 0:00 / 9 2 Destiny’s biggest rival Warframe has had ‘two years of massive growth’ Digital Extremes believes in console growth, and discusses the ‘careful’ development of its second game Christopher Dring Jul 28, 2026 9 2 Share Transcript Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube In This Edition, Digital Extremes’ Sheldon Carter on…

Bungie’s ‘looter shooter’ Destiny was a real thorn in the side of Warframe.

The Digital Extremes game had launched 18 months earlier, and found itself facing off against a better resourced rival.

“There’s a lot of overlap between the two games,” says Digital Extremes president Sheldon Carter.

“Destiny 1 really hit us when it came out. It’s a looter shooter with tons of marketing and really great developers on the team. Destiny 2 as well.”

In May this year, Bungie announced the end of Destiny. It would no longer be making updates to the series. And since then, most of the Destiny team has been laid off.

“For a while we thought about [Destiny] as competition and we were aggressively wanting to compete with what they’re doing. But over time, developers from their team come onto our team. New people who we started, they learnt what looter shooters are because they’ve put thousands of hours into Destiny. And so, at our studio, it was a bit of mourning with that news. The mood was pretty dour.

“The budgets and the competition to keep putting updates out… it’s really difficult and every studio has its own culture and different way of doing things. I can’t imagine [what it’s like] with a studio as big as Bungie, which also had Marathon going on, and a lot of different things pulling them in a lot of directions. Honestly, for me, it’s more sadness that it’s over. I hope the best for all the people there.”

Sheldon Carter, Digital Extremes Warframe is in a very different position. Five years ago, Digital Extremes felt that the game had peaked and it began work on a new game, a multiplayer RPG called Soulframe.

“Some people in the company were like, ‘Oh, Warframe’s peaked. And as it gradually goes to the West, we will have to start something new.” And while we did start another project, we changed our focus about how we were developing Warframe, how we were promoting it, and we’ve had a few years of straight just massive growth.

“Now we’re in this happy position where Warframe’s really thriving, and that gives us the ability to give Soulframe a tone of rope to try stuff out.”

Keywords Studios is the games industry’s end-to-end partner, with over 13,000 people across 26 countries helping studios build, launch and grow games at global scale. Supercharged by technology and shaped by long-term partnership, Keywords Studios connects specialist expertise around the player experience.

For game development, that means flexible production support that scales with ambition. From co-development and engineering to live operations and technical delivery, Keywords Studios helps teams move faster, solve complexity and keep production connected, without losing sight of the game players are waiting for.

Although Warframe lacks the profile of Destiny, the game and its studio is still a significant operation. Digital Extremes, which is owned by Tencent, now has over 500 staff.

items.title: After years of failing to get into MMOs, Warframe finally won me over in 2026
items.content:
Digital Extremes' sci-fi game has finally ensnared me, and I'm now even more excited for Soulframe

The constant updates and endless narrative expansions as seen in World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy 14 intimidate like nothing else in the video game world. I almost always crave the comfort of knowing I'm progressing towards a logical end point – at least when it comes to story-driven games – and the best MMOs , as a rule, seek to go on for eternity.

So despite my efforts, games like Black Desert Online, Fallout 76 , and Genshin Impact lose me soon after I start, simply because I can't accept the potentially limitless experiences on offer. How am I supposed to feel satisfied with my progress if there's no end destination? Well, one game recently changed my mind.

I first tried Warframe over a decade ago on Xbox One but quickly bounced off it. This was a different time in my life, before I could appreciate single-player live service games like Diablo 4 and arguably Fortnite . Even the original Destiny didn't hold my attention, so maybe it was a sci-fi thing? No, that wasn't it – what futuristic FPS could compare to Titanfall back in the day? Or now, for that matter?

But when I went to TennoCon earlier this month, I saw Digital Extremes' long-running epic in a whole new light. The game's community is held in high regard, and it was almost immediately clear as to why. The fans attending the convention were enthusiastic, friendly and generous, praising cosplays and handing out stickers in the name of Warframe and Soulframe, the latter being Digital Extremes' latest work currently in early access on PC only.

As I breathed in the atmosphere, I knew I had to try Warframe again – so I installed the free-to-play title on my Xbox Series X when I got home and jumped in. I chose my first playable biomech warframe (Volt, if you're curious), and began exploring the numerous planets, enemies and loot all crying out for my undivided attention.

In a world filled with live service games, MMORPGs are finding new ways to flourish With wall-running and surprisingly weighty combat, Guild Wars 3 is aiming high: "If we hadn't been making MMOs for 26 years I don't think we could have built this" Guild Wars 3 wants to solve every MMO's biggest problem and might actually pull it off (War)frame of Mind Unlike many of the new games I've been playing in recent years, Warframe is 100% a power fantasy. Right out of the gate, I was blasting foes to bits with firearms, cleaving through them with blades, and electrocuting them with my warframe's unique abilities.

It all felt wonderful. There was no immediate challenge like Elden Ring , or intrinsic sense of vulnerability like Resident Evil Requiem (the Grace sections, anyway). This isn't to say I don't enjoy FromSoftware and Capcom games – because I do – but the change of pace is refreshing in 2026.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

(Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) Image 1 of 4 View Original

As for the all-important narrative element that usually leaves me frustrated in an MMO, I was saved from my usual despair by simply not knowing what was happening. This tracked with what creative director Rebb Ford told GamesRadar+ when we interviewed her recently: "You will have no idea what's going on, and that's okay," she said with a smile, and she was right on the money. Luckily for me, the old adage of 'ignorance is bliss' rang true, because I was having too much fun dishing out damage to care who or what a Tenno was.

So why couldn't I stop worrying and learn how to love the MMO before? In truth, I don't entirely know, but the satisfyingly slick combat and traversal of Warframe certainly plays a part. Each time I begin a mission, I hurl my warframe head-first into the mayhem, shooting, slicing and ability-ing my way through the enemy hordes without a care for why I'm doing it. Yes, I have the guiding voice of Lotus, the game's matriarchal figure (and voiced by Rebb Ford), for support, but I don't pay too much mind to the why , merely the what ..

And yet, my mind wanders from time to time. I think about Lotus, Teshin, and the other NPCs I've made contact with in Digital Extremes' universe, and I want to know their histories, motivations, hopes, and everything else about them. The thing is, I'm in no rush. Warframe has enough content to keep players occupied for a long time – between 114 and 1,556 hours according to How Long to Beat – so I'll find the answers when I'm ready.
